title: Home Assistant 2026.10 Ships Tomorrow — The Open-Source Smart Home Gets Its MCP Moment
key_facts: Home Assistant 2026.10 is due on 7 Oct at 4:00 PM ET, per Forkast News.
It builds the Model Context Protocol (MCP) into the open-source smart-home platform so AI agents can control devices.
A new AI settings page gives a one-click MCP server setup with a copyable URL at /api/mcp, using existing tokens or OAuth.
Forkast says it exposes over 2,000 built-in integrations to agents, and is free and local.
Forkast contrasts it with Google's Home MCP at $20 a month in US early access.
Forkast raises a security question about exposing home controls to third-party agents.
quote_evidence: Home Assistant 2026.10, which officially releases on October 7 at 4:00 PM ET, integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP) directly into the platform.
Exposing your local smart home controls to third-party AI agents via MCP is a powerful convenience, but it requires a new level of vigilance regarding privacy and data access.
why_it_matters_hint: Lets people point an AI of their choice at their home devices without a subscription.
notes: Single outlet, partly opinion; Google pricing and other comparisons are Forkast's. Apple HomePad claims not repeated.
